name: Start Dockerd
description: Deploys the dockerd starter as an on-start hook and runs it once immediately. The pre-baked debian-docker LXC base has docker installed but no init system, so the daemon must be launched explicitly — at deploy time and again on every container start, including after a host reboot. Both moments are served by this one script: `execute_on: "hook"` writes it to /etc/proxvex/on_start.d/ (base64, no heredoc) and triggers it now. It watches the dockerd it started until the socket answers and restarts it with a growing pause (5, 10, 20, 40, 60 s; no new start after 5 min) whenever it dies, because a cold host boot can starve the embedded containerd until dockerd gives up (2026-10-02: 8.99 s to boot, nothing retried; 2026-10-24: died twice in a row, one retry was not enough). The script also wires project-level registry mirrors into /etc/docker/daemon.json (Docker Hub), the LXC nameservers as `dns` upstream in daemon.json (avoids embedded-DNS forwarding glitches in nested LXC-Docker setups), and /etc/hosts (ghcr.io) when the corresponding project defaults are set. Replaces the host-side generator 167-conf-write-dockerd-on-start.json, whose heredoc produced a second, near-identical copy of the same logic. With docker_ipv6 (default on) and an LXC that has IPv6, it also enables IPv6 in dockerd (ULA pools, ip6tables) and sets accept_ra=2 on eth0 so the LXC keeps its SLAAC address once dockerd turns on forwarding.

commands.name: Start Dockerd
commands.description: Deploy dockerd on-start hook (runs at deploy + every container start)
